doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Air National Guard band, then dropping out of USC and UCLA for music
summary: He enlisted in the Air National Guard band during Vietnam, found USC unwelcoming to his ensemble, and on Chuck Berghofer's advice committed to music.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But back to your question, so there was music all around me and I knew it’s what I wanted to do from a very early age I guess. Now I had to — I went into the Air National Guard band based in Van Nuys, actually I did a year in street clothes because the Vietnam War was raging and there wasn’t enough — they didn’t even have uniforms or they couldn’t send me to Basic Training, but I enlisted, it was a year before I even did Basic Training so I did a year in like street clothes rehearsing with this band two times a month — one weekend a month, Saturday and Sunday — and this went on for six years. But it kept me from having to worry about being drafted which of course, this was before the lottery system.

Yeah okay, so you know. So if you either weren’t having a full college load or could convince them that you were nuts, or gay or something that would — or had a serious physical disability, you were drafted. And of course you had the option of enlisting so that’s what I ended up doing. I enlisted in this band. They actually recruited me, to be honest with you. So I did my Basic Training and came back and at that point of course I had the freedom to decide what I wanted to do. I went to USC for — intending to be a © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

music major, but I was so discouraged by the fact that there was no outlet for me to — I asked the professor when I signed up, “What are the chances of me putting together some kind of an ensemble?” I was already doing that. Okay? I already had a little band that I was writing for, kind of a Gil Evansy sort of an instrumentation, eight or nine piece. I forget what it was, band. So I proposed this to this guy, can I continue that kind of activity at an unused room at the school. And the guy looked at me and I swear to you he said, “Well maybe when you’re a senior or a graduate student.” Now I didn’t take very kindly to that. I was not thrilled about the answer. So I did a half a year just doing general ed courses, I think philosophy and logic and a couple of things. And then summer came, because it was in the middle semester, and I thought you know what? Maybe I’ll go to UCLA, never USC, I’ll go to UCLA and enroll in maybe like philosophy or psychology or something, something to fall back on. And you know what happened? I went there to enroll, to register for the classes, to this giant campus where I’d be walking around endless I don’t know miles, see it looked like miles to me, to take these courses. And I just thought you know what? This is not what I want to do. And of course I was starting to work so I had a little conference with my parents and also I remember sitting at Donte’s jazz club with Chuck Berghofer, a great bass player, and asking, “Chuck, what do you think I should do?” And Chuck says, “Hey, if you want to do music you should do it.” And I never looked back.
